Colleges, universities, and other educational institutions are also encouraging their students to get career guidance. Students are also required to receive mandatory guidance and IT career counseling from their schools as part of their education to help them choose a proper career path. When students are counseled using fingerprint reports, their career options are more clear since they are choosing careers based on their skills and abilities. The Information Technology (IT) sector supports many other sectors, enabling them to easily complete their daily tasks and routines, allowing both governmental and private sectors to operate smoothly. Occupational opportunities in IT include implementing software, building hardware, managing multimedia, and integrating complex systems. Having a revolutionary effect on society and the economy, the IT industry is dynamic and entrepreneurship-driven. Besides IT careers in the IT industry, IT careers are also available in other areas of the economy, including financial services, medical services, business, and engineering. A career here will suit you if you are skilled at using cutting-edge technology. It is common for many IT professionals/students to think that as computer science or IT students their job is simply programming, however, programming is only a tool for solving problems. Solving the problem is the primary requirement.
